result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.get_max_eccentricity()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Get maximum eccentricity (graph diameter). ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L44171-L44221){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.get_max_eccentricity(unconnected=True) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Maximum eccentricity](/assets/graphs/get-max-eccentricity.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="A six-node graph with each node's eccentricity in a badge: A 4, B 3, C 2, D 2, E 3, F 4. The end nodes A and F have the largest value and are drawn in the accent color; the card gives the maximum eccentricity 4." width="100%"} Alias for `get_diameter()`. The maximum eccentricity is the longest shortest path between any two nodes. A node's eccentricity is the number of hops to the farthest node it can reach; the nodes with the largest eccentricity form the *periphery* of the graph, and their eccentricity is the longest distance anything in the network ever has to travel. Distances are counted in hops (edge weights are ignored) and, in directed graphs, follow edge directions. See `get_diameter()` for details. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [unconnected]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Controls what happens when some nodes cannot reach each other. If `True` (default), each node's eccentricity only considers the nodes it can reach, so the result is the largest diameter among the connected components. If `False`, returns `None` unless every node can reach every other (strong connectivity for directed graphs). ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [int | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Maximum eccentricity (diameter), or `None` if disconnected (when `unconnected=False`). Also `None` for an empty graph. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} In a path of five nodes the two ends are four hops apart, so the maximum eccentricity is `4`: ::: {#1e981e02 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph().add_path_graph(5) graph.get_max_eccentricity() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 4 ``` ::: ::: Joining the ends into a cycle halves the longest trip; the result always matches `get_diameter()`: ::: {#2bf4c501 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} ring = ec.Graph().add_cycle_graph(5) (ring.get_max_eccentricity(), ring.get_diameter()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` (2, 2) ``` ::: :::
